title: Synchronized deployment slate and cutover playbook for runtime / console / API surfaces
creator: Lena Morales
description: Create a single, actionable playbook and deployment slate that coordinates runtime, Console, and public API releases across sprint boundaries. The goal is to reduce cross-team merge/rollout friction, minimize customer-visible regressions during multi-surface launches, and provide a deterministic cutover procedure for high-risk changes (kernel swaps, large KV cache migrations, schema changes, infra upgrades).
acceptance_criteria: A concise deployment slate format (CSV/JSON + Slack template) exists and is adopted by Eng/PM leads for all multi-surface releases
Cutover playbook includes: preflight checklist, canary schedule, rollback criteria, post-cutover validations, and escalation matrix
At least two pilot releases (one runtime-heavy, one console-heavy) use the playbook end-to-end with postmortem and <10% deviation from planned windows
All required monitoring dashboards and synthetic checks referenced in playbook are created and linked
Runbook owners and primary/secondary on-call contacts listed for each step
milestones: Draft playbook & slate template (owned by PM) — 2026-02-27
Pilot #2 (console UI feature + API contract change) — 2026-03-18
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large runtime kernel change may introduce latency spikes — Mitigation: reserve dedicated canary capacity and run 1-hour production shadowing prior to cutover
Risk: Console migration may depend on API contract bump — Mitigation: feature-flag all console-facing changes and publish backwards-compatible API adapters for 2 cycles
Risk: Cross-team merge collisions during freeze windows — Mitigation: use slate to enforce merge embargo and a single-point-of-contact for emergency merges
Risk: Monitoring gaps for new surface checks — Mitigation: add synthetic probes and alert playbook before the cutover window; block cutover until green for 1h
notes_and_links: Related Linear ticket: PM-24011 (release-train-contingency-lanes) — reference policies
